summary: Richard Jay Kohn was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1988 under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, also studying under Lama Tharchin Rinpoche.

Richard K. Payne is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies who studied under Chisei Aratano and Taisen Miyata. He served as Dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1996–2019), with later affiliations at GTU and the University of Chicago.
Richard Keith Sprigg was a linguist and Tibetologist who studied at Oakham School. He held posts at the University of London and SOAS University of London from circa 1948 to 1980.

Richard Kieckhefer is a historian and religious studies scholar educated at Saint Louis University and the University of Texas at Austin (PhD 1972). He held posts at Monumenta Germaniae Historica and joined Northwestern University in 1975.

Richard King is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology who studied at Dalhousie, McGill, and Lancaster University (PhD 1992). He held posts at the University of Stirling, Vanderbilt University, and the University of Glasgow.

Richard M. Jaffe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He held academic posts at North Carolina State University from circa 1995 to 2000 and at Duke University around 2000.

Richard Mahoney is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Paul Harrison at the University of Canterbury, where he completed his Master of Arts in 2002 and held a post attested in 2001.

Richard Morris was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Battersea. He taught at King's College School and Dedham Grammar School, later serving as headmaster of the Royal Masonic School for Boys (1875–1888).

Richard P. Boyle pursued graduate work at the University of Washington and studied under Kyozan Joshu Sasaki. He taught at the University of California, Los Angeles, and was later affiliated with the University of New Mexico.

Richard P. Hayes is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology who earned his doctorate from the University of Toronto. He held posts at Toronto, McGill University, Leiden University, and the University of New Mexico.
Richard Peter Hottelet is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Narayan Hemandas Samtani and held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, attested in 1971.
Richard Phené Spiers was an architect and historian who studied at King's College London from circa 1856 to 1858 and at the École Nationale Supérieure des Beaux-Arts from circa 1858 to 1861.

Richard Pischel was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Promotion and Habilitation at Breslau. He held professorships at the University of Kiel, Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1885–1902), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1902–1908).

Richard Polenberg was an American history scholar educated at Brooklyn College and Columbia University (PhD 1964). He served as a professor at Cornell University from 1966 to 2011 and was a Fulbright Visiting Professor at Hebrew University.

Richard Rorty was a philosopher educated at the University of Chicago and Yale University. He held professorships at Wellesley College, Princeton University (ca. 1962–1982), the University of Virginia (1982–1998), and Stanford University starting in 1998.

Richard Salomon is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Ludo Rocher. He held a professorship at the University of Washington, attested between 1998 and 2017, and was a visiting researcher at Soka University in 2007.

Richard Schmidt was an Indologist who completed his doctorate and habilitation at Halle-Wittenberg under Richard Pischel and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He taught at Halle-Wittenberg and served as ordinary professor at the University of Münster from 1910.

Richard Shilleto was a classicist active in linguistics and history. He was educated at Repton School, Shrewsbury School, and Trinity College, Cambridge, graduating around 1832, and later taught Robert Alexander Neil.

Richard Sorabji is a philosopher and Indologist educated at Pembroke College, Oxford. He held academic posts at Cornell University (circa 1962–1970), King's College London (circa 1970–2000), and Gresham College (circa 2000–2006).

Richard Sproat is a linguist educated at the University of California, San Diego, and MIT (PhD 1985). He held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (2003–2009), Oregon Health and Science University (2009–2012), and Google in 2012.
